subject: history
title: MAIN Causes of World War I
welcome_lead: From the Balkans to the trenches, examine why Europe blundered into industrialised slaughter in 1914.
meta_desc: History Causes & Effects of Wars Adventure 1: long-term and short-term causes of the First World War.
final_note: You have surveyed the powder keg of pre-1914 Europe. Causation in history is always multi-layered.

concepts.def: Glorification of armed forces and willingness to use them, expressed in the pre-1914 arms race.
Pre-1914 system tying powers to mutual defence: Triple Entente vs Triple Alliance.
Great-power competition for colonies and spheres of influence that heightened tensions.
Belief in the nation-state which inflamed both Great Power rivalries and Balkan separatism.
German strategy to defeat France quickly through Belgium before turning east against Russia.
Diplomatic sequence in 1914 after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand that led to general war.

walkthroughs.body_html: Historians often summarise the long-term causes with the acronym MAIN: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism and Nationalism. The Anglo-German naval race (HMS Dreadnought, 1906), competing colonial empires, the Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) opposing the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and ethno-nationalist tensions in the Balkans all contributed to fragility.

The Moroccan crises of 1905 and 1911, the Bosnian Annexation Crisis of 1908 and the Balkan Wars of 1912-13 entrenched rivalries. The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914 by Gavrilo Princip triggered the July Crisis. Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia, Russian mobilisation and German implementation of the Schlieffen Plan rapidly internationalised the conflict.

Interpretations range from Fritz Fischer's claim that Germany deliberately willed war to Christopher Clark's Sleepwalkers, emphasising shared responsibility and miscalculation. candidates should weigh structural and contingent factors and consider how decisions in Berlin, Vienna, St Petersburg, Paris and London each contributed.
